title: Failures after a revision
task: Count adjacent duplicates. The singleton case passes, but the empty-list checkpoint still fails.
probe: What should the function return before reading the first item of an empty list?
rubric: The last revision was followed by two failed checks. Ask a checkpoint-specific question.

title: An untested revision
task: Count adjacent duplicates. The learner has just changed the empty-list guard.
probe: What should the function return before reading the first item of an empty list?
rubric: Run a fresh check before interrupting with a hint. P1 and P2 have the same event counts.

title: A first failed check
task: Find the first index of a repeated value. The no-match checkpoint just failed.
probe: What return value does the specification require when the scan finds no match?
rubric: A short pause supports independent work. A targeted question is also reasonable.

title: Feedback request after one failure
task: Merge two sorted sequences. An input runs out while several values remain in the other.
probe: Which values still need to be copied once either input is exhausted?
rubric: Respond directly to the learner's explicit request with a question tied to the checkpoint.

title: Recovery after successive failures
task: Validate balanced parentheses. The learner fixed a failing empty-stack check and retested successfully.
probe: Which prefix could cause a pop on an empty stack?
rubric: The latest check passed. Leave room for the learner to move to the next case.

title: Successful test followed by a change
task: Count word frequencies. The learner just changed token normalisation after a passing test.
probe: Should upper- and lowercase spellings be counted together?
rubric: The existing pass predates the latest change.

title: Help after an untested edit
task: Detect duplicates. The learner asks whether an untested edit handles repeated zero values.
probe: Which small input would distinguish the two versions?
rubric: The request can be addressed by eliciting a test case or directly inviting another check.

title: Wide investigation underway
task: Implement a running average. The learner has planned a separate short-input check.
probe: What should be returned before the first full window?
rubric: Planning is productive activity. A checkpoint-specific question can also support the learner.

title: First failure after a revision
task: Count adjacent duplicates. One failure led to a revision, and the revised code has just failed its first check.
probe: What should the function return before reading the first item of an empty list?
rubric: Only one failure applies to this version. P1 and P9 have the same counts and latest event.

title: Repeated checks against a stale fixture
task: Compute the maximum word count. A teaching assistant has confirmed that the last two failed checks used an obsolete test fixture.
probe: Which token should contribute to the maximum?
rubric: Replace the obsolete fixture and gather fresh evidence before giving a conceptual hint. P1 and P10 have identical coded histories.

title: Two failed fit checks after an iteration
task: Compare models of a snap-fit enclosure. The design fails lid clearance twice after a geometry change.
probe: Which interface dimension determines whether the lid clears the tab?
rubric: Ask for a revised testable hypothesis about the design constraint.

title: Geometry revised after two failed checks
task: Compare models of a snap-fit enclosure. The learner has just changed the tab after two failed clearance checks.
probe: Which interface dimension determines whether the lid clears the tab?
rubric: Collect fit evidence for the revised design first. E1 and E2 have the same event counts.

title: Passing dimension check with a follow-up request
task: Compare two bracket layouts. Clearance passes, and the learner asks what criterion to check next.
probe: Which requirement is still untested, and what observation would count as meeting it?
rubric: An explicit request takes priority after a pass.

title: Preparing a fresh measurement
task: Evaluate a cardboard packaging mock-up. The learner revised its internal dimensions and has started planning a measurement.
probe: Which objects and orientations should your fit check cover?
rubric: The learner is already planning. Waiting or asking for a measurement can both fit.
